title: Paywalled extraction: fetch through a real logged-in browser profile (DataDome blocks the headless cookie path)
body:
## Evidence (2026-10-06, Homelab, image 867e6a237dc6)

- #149's scoped exception is deployed and active: `ARGUS_AUTH_BROWSER_DOMAINS=nytimes.com,wsj.com,…`. The log shows `Browser admitted without network attestation via ARGUS_AUTH_BROWSER_DOMAINS host=www.nytimes.com`.
- NYT: a fresh export installed today (`/data/cookies/nytimes.com.json`, 24 live cookies, `NYT-S` valid to 2027-10-06) still gets `Auth failed … (HTTP 403)`. A plain request from Homelab gets NYT's DataDome challenge with no cookies, all cookies, or `NYT-S` alone.
- WSJ: `extract_content_v2` request `933659242b13427c` failed. Trafilatura got HTTP 401 and the auth path was not used. `wsj.com.json` (Sep 13) has no live session cookie: of 60 cookies, the 43 live ones are tracking/consent cookies plus a `datadome` cookie.
- `/data/cookies/health.json` has marked every paywall domain `stale` (403/401) since Sep 14: NYT, WSJ, Bloomberg, Stratechery.
- Egress is already residential, so the blocker is the browser fingerprint, not the IP. `auth_extractor` launches `chromium.launch(headless=True)` and claims a Mac Chrome 131 user agent on Linux. DataDome detects that.

## Decision

Do not try to beat DataDome's bot check from headless Chromium. Use a real browser with a persistent profile that the owner logs in to once, as g2k's ChatGPT web lane already does on Homelab (`deploy/homelab/g2k-chatgpt-browser.{service,sh}`, `g2k-cdp-guard.nft`, login with `g2k-web-login view <display>` over an SSH-tunnelled noVNC).

## Plan

1. Homelab: add a `argus-paywall-browser` user service. It runs real Chromium (not headless) on its own Xvfb display, with a persistent profile under the argus state directory. CDP listens on loopback/bridge only and is guarded the same way as `g2k-cdp-guard`.
2. Argus: add `ARGUS_AUTH_BROWSER_CDP_URL`. When it is set, `auth_extractor` connects over CDP and opens pages in the browser's existing default context (`browser.contexts[0]`), so the profile's own login is used. It does not create a new context, inject cookies or override the user agent. Close the tab after each extraction. The cookie-file path stays as the fallback.
3. The owner logs in to NYT and WSJ once in that browser over noVNC. After that, the exported cookie files are no longer needed for those domains (delete them and the `.bak`).
4. Acceptance: one paywalled NYT article and one WSJ article through `extract_content_v2` return full text. Then Atlas #47 re-runs its 18 saves.

Filed from g2k's session (Atlas #44 follow-up).

Update `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, and `docs/INFRA.md` (or equivalent) to document the mise adoption: exact source (Infra727), the pinned Python version and why, the interpreter path configuration, the lock generation command and platform list, and the evidence from focused checks. title: Migrate CI pipeline to use mise tasks
body:
Parent issue: #177

## What
Update CI workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`) to install mise, trust the project config, and invoke test/lint/typecheck via `mise run` instead of direct `uv run` or `make` calls. Pin the mise version. Keep the same Python version, dependency cache keys, and artifact uploads. Do not change deploy workflows.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CI installs mise with a pinned version
- [ ] CI runs `mise trust` before invoking tasks
- [ ] Test, lint, and typecheck jobs use `mise run <task>`
- [ ] Python version in CI matches the mise-pinned version
- [ ] Dependency cache keys and artifact uploads are preserved
- [ ] Deploy workflows are unchanged
- [ ] CI passes on a fresh worktree

title: Define mise tasks wrapping existing dev workflows
body:
Parent issue: #177

## What
Add `[tasks]` entries to `mise.toml` that wrap the project's existing Make targets and scripts (install, test, lint, typecheck, format, clean). Each task calls the existing Make target or script directly — no logic duplication. Tasks must work via `mise run <task>` and `mise exec -- <command>`. Preserve all existing Make/script behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `[tasks]` section defines tasks for: install/sync, test, lint, typecheck, format, clean
- [ ] Each task invokes the existing Make target or script (e.g., `make test`)
- [ ] `mise run test` produces identical output to `make test`
- [ ] `mise run install` creates `.venv` using the mise-managed Python
- [ ] All existing Make targets and scripts remain unchanged
- [ ] `mise tasks` lists all defined tasks

title: Generate uv.lock metadata for intended platforms
body:
Parent issue: #177

## What
Run `uv lock` with `--python-platform` flags for the platforms CI targets (linux x86_64, linux aarch64, macos aarch64) to generate multi-platform lock metadata. Do not claim platforms were executed — only that lock generation succeeded. Record the exact command and platform list in a comment or docs. The lock must remain consistent with existing `pyproject.toml` dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `uv lock --python-platform linux-x86_64 --python-platform linux-aarch64 --python-platform macos-aarch64` succeeds
- [ ] `uv.lock` contains entries for all three target platforms
- [ ] `uv lock --check` passes (lock is up-to-date with pyproject.toml)
- [ ] Exact command and platform list documented in mise.toml comment or docs/INFRA.md
- [ ] No dependency version changes beyond what multi-platform resolution requires

- [ ] Prior environment remains intact as rollback

global shell activation, old-venv removal and runtime-manager retirement. Keep
native macOS/ML and release-controller environments under their own acceptance
paths. Return a reviewed source PR; a passing development environment does not
prove production cutover or authorize lifting an existing merge hold.

title: feat: add opt-in sanitized Tavily credential metadata observation
body:
## Summary

```text
existing 30-minute authority probe loop
  opt-in false -> no observation I/O
  opt-in true -> fixed Tavily usage metadata GET (one attempt)
    bounded typed outcomes -> atomic redacted latest receipt
```

Homelab H26 needs owner-produced credential evidence without exporting
credentials. This first slice observes Tavily metadata with the existing key
and data mount, and leaves overall health unknown. It adds no search, model
operation, grant, daemon or consumer contract change. Definition/source identity
and typed unknown outcomes are explicit; no raw usage/account/provider response
is persisted. The filesystem boundary refuses unsafe leaves and preserves
pre-rename state; post-rename durability failure remains unknown.

## Evidence

- **Before:** adversarial tests exposed unbounded/malformed input and unsafe
  filesystem publication, then a floating-point attempt admission defect.
  **After:** 69 observer/configuration/API lifecycle tests, focused Ruff and
  independent final review pass after corrections.
- Explicit opt-in remains false. Production remains source `e8f36cf` and its
  accepted `c8853fbe` image with four protected overrides. Guarded image/source
  admission, backup/restore, rollback and the required soak precede enablement.
  Natural producer, independently bound consumer, durable log and notification
  acceptance remain separate TODO gates.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The producer is disabled by default. Deploy through the existing digest/source
promotion path; preserve protected overrides and provider holds.

**Blast Radius:** observer

title: fix: stabilize restored Atlas constraint inventory
body:
## Summary

```diff

- hash PostgreSQL's raw CHECK text after dump/restore
+ canonicalize only equivalent literal text-array ANY casts before hashing
```

The guarded #162 promotion passed its candidate gates but failed closed at Atlas restore inventory. A disposable restore isolated two equivalent `dispatch_receipts` CHECK deparse strings as the only schema difference. This change keeps the restore gate and requires a fresh immutable backup; it does not edit old manifests or deploy Argus.

- **Before:** `restored database does not match source inventory` after archive SHA checks passed. Atlas table counts and all other inspected schema categories matched.
  **After:** regression cases normalize both PostgreSQL spellings and still reject a changed literal.
- Python 3.12 focused recovery suite: 85 passed, 20 skipped. Ruff `F` checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Diagnosis: `docs/evidence/2026-09-29-restore-inventory-debug.md`.
